concept.title: What is a Password Manager
concept.shortdesc: How do password managers help you generate, store, and manage strong, unique passwords while improving overall account security.

conbody.p: Strong passwords, those that are long, random, and unique, are essential to personal and university cybersecurity, but memorizing a distinct complex password for every online account is impractical. Storing passwords as plaintext in physical notes or unencrypted digital files exposes your accounts if your device is lost or compromised. A password manager solves this problem by generating strong, random passwords, autofilling login fields, and encrypting your credentials in a vault protected by a single master password and multi-factor authentication (MFA). When selecting a vetted password manager, verify compatibility across all of your devices and decide between cloud-based storage (which syncs across devices over the internet) or a locally maintained database (which stays on your device and requires regular backups to separate storage media).
conbody.note: NC State staff and faculty must use only university-approved password management tools for storing institutional credentials, whereas students may select vetted personal password managers for their non-university accounts.
